key_insight: A parameter-free ab initio transport framework can predict charge mobility in molecular semiconductors by simulating full electron–phonon dynamics, revealing the dominant transport mechanism directly from atomic structure.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable screening and design of organic transistor and photovoltaic materials by linking molecular structure to measurable mobility, temperature dependence, and optical response.
method: Compute electron–phonon Hamiltonians from first principles
Propagate carriers in large molecular domains with the full phonon spectrum
Use nonperturbative Green–Kubo dynamics to let transport regimes emerge
evidence_signal: The framework was benchmarked across five representative crystals and reproduced measured mobilities, temperature exponents, and optical-conductivity fingerprints.
watch_item: The approach is computationally demanding and still depends on the quality of the underlying ab initio electron–phonon calculations and material models.
paper_title: First-Principles Origins of Charge Transport in Molecular Semiconductors
